_meta.description: Curated offline catalogue of publicly reported data breaches.
_meta.note: Compiled from public reporting. Figures are the widely-reported account/record counts and may be approximate or disputed by the companies involved. Entries marked disputed=true were denied or contested by the organisation.
_meta.count_note: This is an offline reference catalogue, not a live feed.

breaches.name: Yahoo
breaches.desc: The largest breach ever disclosed. All 3 billion Yahoo accounts were compromised. Disclosed only in 2016-2017.

breaches.name: Yahoo (2014 incident)
breaches.desc: A separate state-sponsored intrusion affecting 500 million accounts.

breaches.name: Aadhaar (reported exposure)
breaches.desc: Journalists reported broker access to Aadhaar data via insecure third-party endpoints. UIDAI disputed that its core database was breached.

breaches.name: Alibaba / Taobao
breaches.desc: A developer scraped Taobao over eight months using crawler software.

breaches.name: LinkedIn (2021 scrape)
breaches.desc: Scraped public profile data for 92% of LinkedIn users offered for sale.

breaches.name: Sina Weibo
breaches.desc: Account details for 538 million users offered on a dark web marketplace.

breaches.name: Facebook
breaches.desc: Data scraped via a contact-import vulnerability, published free in 2021. Covers 106 countries including 6 million Indian users.

breaches.name: Yahoo Japan
breaches.desc: Suspected unauthorised access to user ID records.

breaches.name: Friend Finder Networks
breaches.desc: Twenty years of data across six adult/dating sites. Highly sensitive due to the nature of the sites.

breaches.name: Marriott / Starwood
breaches.desc: Four years of undetected access to the Starwood reservation system, including 5.25 million unencrypted passport numbers.

breaches.name: MySpace
breaches.desc: Weak unsalted SHA-1 hashes, trivially cracked. Surfaced publicly in 2016.

breaches.name: Exactis
breaches.desc: A marketing data broker left a database publicly accessible with roughly 400 fields per person.

breaches.name: Twitter (2022 scrape)
breaches.desc: Scraped via an API vulnerability that let attackers link email addresses to accounts.

breaches.name: Deezer
breaches.desc: Taken from a third-party service provider, published in late 2022.

breaches.name: NetEase
breaches.desc: Account details from the Chinese email provider offered for sale.

breaches.name: Wattpad
breaches.desc: The storytelling platform's user database was offered on hacking forums.

breaches.name: Zynga
breaches.desc: Draw Something and Words With Friends player accounts.

breaches.name: LinkedIn (2012 breach)
breaches.desc: Initially thought to be 6.5 million; the full 164 million surfaced in 2016. Unsalted SHA-1 made cracking trivial.

breaches.name: Dubsmash
breaches.desc: Sold on the Dream Market dark web marketplace.

breaches.name: Adobe
breaches.desc: Passwords were encrypted with a reversible cipher rather than hashed, and plaintext password hints were included.

breaches.name: Equifax
breaches.desc: An unpatched Apache Struts vulnerability exposed the most sensitive financial identity data of nearly half the US population.

breaches.name: eBay
breaches.desc: Attackers used stolen employee credentials to access the user database.

breaches.name: MyFitnessPal
breaches.desc: Under Armour's fitness app. Some passwords used weak SHA-1 hashing.

breaches.name: Canva
breaches.desc: The design platform was breached by the GnosticPlayers group.

breaches.name: Badoo
breaches.desc: Dating service account data with weak MD5 hashing.

breaches.name: Gravatar
breaches.desc: Profile data scraped via an enumerable API. Gravatar MD5 hashes are easily reversed for common addresses.

breaches.name: Capital One
breaches.desc: A misconfigured web application firewall allowed access to AWS S3 credit application data.

breaches.name: Quora
breaches.desc: Unauthorised access by a malicious third party.

breaches.name: JustDial
breaches.desc: An unprotected API exposed user records in real time.

breaches.name: MobiKwik
breaches.desc: Researchers reported 8.2 TB of KYC and payment data for sale. MobiKwik denied a breach occurred.

breaches.name: VK (VKontakte)
breaches.desc: Passwords were stored in plaintext.

breaches.name: MyHeritage
breaches.desc: The genealogy service's user table was found on a private server.

breaches.name: Tokopedia
breaches.desc: Indonesia's largest e-commerce platform.

breaches.name: Facebook / Cambridge Analytica
breaches.desc: Profile data harvested through a personality quiz app and used for political targeting.

breaches.name: Nitro PDF
breaches.desc: Document records and user data offered at auction.

breaches.name: Edmodo
breaches.desc: An education platform used widely by schools, so many affected accounts belonged to minors.

breaches.name: T-Mobile
breaches.desc: One of several repeated T-Mobile breaches. Highly useful for SIM-swap attacks.

breaches.name: Collection #1
breaches.desc: A 87 GB aggregated compilation of credentials from thousands of earlier breaches, purpose-built for credential-stuffing attacks.

breaches.name: RockYou
breaches.desc: Passwords stored in plaintext. The resulting wordlist is still the single most-used password-cracking dictionary in the world.

breaches.name: RockYou2024 compilation
breaches.desc: A compilation of nearly 10 billion unique plaintext passwords aggregated from historical breaches. Not account data, but the definitive cracking wordlist.

breaches.name: National Public Data
breaches.desc: A background-check data broker leaked billions of records including Social Security numbers, affecting people who never used the service.

breaches.name: Ticketmaster
breaches.desc: Linked to the wider Snowflake-related campaign targeting cloud data warehouses.

breaches.name: AT&T (call records)
breaches.desc: Six months of call and text metadata for nearly all AT&T mobile customers, taken from a Snowflake workspace.

breaches.name: AT&T (customer data)
breaches.desc: Historical customer data including account passcodes surfaced on a hacking forum.

breaches.name: MOVEit Transfer campaign
breaches.desc: A zero-day in the MOVEit file-transfer product let the Cl0p group steal data from over 2,700 organisations.

breaches.name: Change Healthcare
breaches.desc: A ransomware attack that disrupted US healthcare payments nationwide and exposed highly sensitive medical data.

breaches.name: Dropbox
breaches.desc: Caused by an employee reusing a password that had been exposed in the LinkedIn breach.

breaches.name: Tumblr
breaches.desc: Salted SHA-1 hashes, disclosed publicly in 2016.

breaches.name: Neopets
breaches.desc: Source code and the full user database were stolen. Weak unsalted MD5 hashing.

breaches.name: Uber
breaches.desc: Uber paid the attackers $100,000 to delete the data and concealed the breach for over a year.

breaches.name: Houzz
breaches.desc: Publicly disclosed in early 2019.

breaches.name: Last.fm
breaches.desc: Unsalted MD5 hashes made password recovery nearly instant.

breaches.name: ShareThis
breaches.desc: Part of the GnosticPlayers collection.

breaches.name: Chegg
breaches.desc: The education technology company used weak unsalted MD5 hashing.

breaches.name: T-Mobile (2023)
breaches.desc: Accessed through a vulnerable API over several weeks before detection.

breaches.name: Poshmark
breaches.desc: Social commerce marketplace user data.

breaches.name: Star Health Insurance
breaches.desc: Customer medical records and identity documents were leaked through Telegram chatbots. Extremely sensitive health data.

breaches.name: Internet Archive
breaches.desc: The site was also defaced and hit by DDoS attacks at the same time.

breaches.name: Ashley Madison
breaches.desc: The infidelity dating site. The breach led to extortion campaigns and several reported suicides. A landmark case in breach harm.

breaches.name: Zoosk
breaches.desc: Dating service user records offered for sale.

breaches.name: Mathway
breaches.desc: Maths-solving app user accounts.

breaches.name: Animoto
breaches.desc: Video creation service.

breaches.name: Unacademy
breaches.desc: India's largest online learning platform. Accounts included staff from major corporations.

breaches.name: BigBasket
breaches.desc: India's online grocery leader. Data offered for sale for about $40,000.

breaches.name: 8fit
breaches.desc: Fitness app accounts, part of the GnosticPlayers collection.

breaches.name: Domino's India
breaches.desc: 180 million order records including precise delivery locations were published on a searchable website.

breaches.name: Disqus
breaches.desc: The commenting platform's user database, disclosed in 2017.

breaches.name: Zomato
breaches.desc: The restaurant discovery platform. The attacker returned the data after Zomato agreed to run a bug bounty programme.

breaches.name: 000webhost
breaches.desc: All passwords were stored in plaintext with no hashing whatsoever.

breaches.name: Bukalapak
breaches.desc: Indonesian e-commerce marketplace.

breaches.name: Armor Games
breaches.desc: Online gaming portal.

breaches.name: Optus
breaches.desc: An unauthenticated public API exposed Australian identity documents, triggering mass document reissuance.

breaches.name: Medibank
breaches.desc: Attackers published sensitive medical procedure data when the ransom was refused.

breaches.name: Teespring
breaches.desc: Custom apparel marketplace.

breaches.name: boAt Lifestyle
breaches.desc: India's leading audio wearables brand. Customer data posted on a hacking forum.

breaches.name: Robinhood
breaches.desc: Obtained through social engineering of a customer support employee.

breaches.name: 23andMe
breaches.desc: Credential stuffing against accounts that reused breached passwords exposed genetic ancestry data, including lists targeting specific ethnic groups.

breaches.name: Air India
breaches.desc: Via a breach of the SITA passenger service system used by many airlines.

breaches.name: Minted
breaches.desc: Design marketplace user records sold by ShinyHunters.

breaches.name: Upstox
breaches.desc: The stockbroking platform confirmed KYC data was accessed from a third-party warehouse.

breaches.name: Pixlr
breaches.desc: Online photo editor, leaked alongside the 123RF breach.

breaches.name: LastPass
breaches.desc: Attackers stole encrypted vault backups. Vaults with weak master passwords can be cracked offline, and website URLs were not encrypted.

breaches.name: Twitch
breaches.desc: 125 GB of internal data leaked, including three years of creator earnings. User passwords were reported as not exposed.

breaches.name: SolarWinds Orion
breaches.desc: A supply-chain compromise that distributed a backdoored update to around 18,000 organisations including US federal agencies.

breaches.name: AIIMS Delhi
breaches.desc: A ransomware attack crippled India's premier hospital for weeks and exposed patient data including that of VIPs.

breaches.name: CDSL (Central Depository Services)
breaches.desc: A misconfiguration exposed investor KYC data for over 43 million Indian demat account holders.

breaches.name: Policybazaar
breaches.desc: The insurance aggregator disclosed illegal access to its systems. The number of affected records was not published.

breaches.name: WazirX
breaches.desc: A multi-signature wallet compromise resulted in approximately $235 million in cryptocurrency being stolen from the Indian exchange.

breaches.name: RentoMojo
breaches.desc: The furniture rental startup confirmed unauthorised database access.

breaches.name: Jio (reported)
breaches.desc: Subscriber data appeared on a searchable website. Reliance Jio disputed the authenticity of the data.

breaches.name: Dell
breaches.desc: A partner portal API was abused to scrape customer purchase records.

breaches.name: Marriott (2020)
breaches.desc: A second Marriott incident, via compromised employee franchise credentials.

breaches.name: Evite
breaches.desc: The online invitation service's legacy database was sold on the dark web.

breaches.name: Imgur
breaches.desc: Disclosed in 2017. Imgur had already migrated to bcrypt by then.

breaches.name: Mashable
breaches.desc: A database of readers who used social login was leaked.

breaches.name: CoffeeMeetsBagel
breaches.desc: Dating app user records, part of the GnosticPlayers collection.

breaches.name: Ixigo
breaches.desc: The Indian travel booking platform's user database was offered for sale.

breaches.name: Whitepages
breaches.desc: People-search directory records.

breaches.name: Bonobos
breaches.desc: A 70 GB cloud backup of the clothing retailer was published on a hacking forum.

provider_notes.gmail.com: Google itself has not suffered a mass password breach, but Gmail addresses appear in nearly every third-party breach because Gmail is the world's most used consumer email provider.
provider_notes.yahoo.com: Yahoo suffered the two largest breaches in history (3 billion and 500 million accounts). If you have ever had a Yahoo account, assume it was affected.
provider_notes.ymail.com: Part of Yahoo Mail and covered by the Yahoo breaches.
provider_notes.rocketmail.com: A legacy Yahoo Mail domain, covered by the Yahoo breaches.
provider_notes.hotmail.com: A legacy Microsoft domain. No mass Microsoft password breach, but these addresses are old and therefore appear in many historical third-party breaches.
provider_notes.outlook.com: Microsoft has not suffered a mass consumer password breach, but these addresses appear widely in third-party breaches.
provider_notes.live.com: A Microsoft domain with the same exposure profile as Outlook and Hotmail.
provider_notes.aol.com: AOL suffered a breach in 2014 affecting a reported 2% of accounts, and these are among the oldest consumer addresses in circulation.
provider_notes.rediffmail.com: A long-established Indian provider. Addresses are typically old and appear in many historical breaches.
provider_notes.protonmail.com: Privacy-focused with no mass breach history, but the address can still appear in any third-party service breach.
provider_notes.proton.me: Privacy-focused with no mass breach history, but the address can still appear in any third-party service breach.
provider_notes.icloud.com: Apple has not suffered a mass password breach. The 2014 celebrity iCloud incident was targeted credential theft, not a database breach.
provider_notes.zoho.com: No mass breach history. Common for business use in India.
provider_notes.mail.com: No mass breach history, but frequently used for throwaway registrations.
provider_notes.yandex.com: Yandex disclosed an insider data incident in 2021 affecting around 4,900 mailboxes.
